content: The content provided appears to be a detailed reference list and dosage guidelines for the treatment of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB). 1. Jacobson et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in 2013 to evaluate treatment outcomes in patients with extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB). Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 2. Gandhi et al. reported that XDR-TB is a significant cause of mortality in patients co-infected with tuberculosis and HIV in rural South Africa. This study was published in The Lancet. 3. Leung et al. investigated the transmission of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and XDR-TB in a metropolitan city, with their findings published in the European Respiratory Journal. 4. Shah et al. explored the transmission dynamics of XDR-TB in South Africa, with their research published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 5. Maryandyshev et al. described the use of a combination of bedaquiline and delamanid in treating five patients with pulmonary XDR-TB. This case series was published in Emerging Infectious Diseases. 6. Migliori et al. conducted a systematic review on the combined use of delamanid and bedaquiline for treating MDR and XDR-TB, with their findings published in the International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 7. Ferlazzo et al. assessed the early safety and efficacy of bedaquiline and delamanid combination therapy in patients with drug-resistant TB in Armenia, India, and South Africa. This retrospective cohort study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 8. Donald reviewed the chemotherapy of tuberculous meningitis in children and adults, with the findings published in Tuberculosis in 2010. 9. Sun et al. demonstrated the rapid and dramatic therapeutic effects of linezolid in patients with life-threatening tuberculous meningitis. This study was published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy. 10. Thwaites et al. conducted a randomized pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic comparison of fluoroquinolones for tuberculous meningitis, with their findings published in Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy. 11. The Curry International Tuberculosis Center and the California Department of Public Health published a survival guide for clinicians managing drug-resistant tuberculosis. 12. Daley reviewed the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex in the context of antimicrobial therapy and vaccines, as published in a textbook by Williams & Wilkins. 13. Holdiness explored the cerebrospinal fluid pharmacokinetics of antituberculosis drugs, with findings published in Clinical Pharmacokinetics. 14. Loveday et al. examined maternal and infant outcomes among pregnant women treated for MDR/RR-TB in South Africa, with their findings published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 15. Mitnick et al. highlighted the importance of monitoring intervals and microbiological methods in detecting treatment failure in MDR-TB, as published in the European Respiratory Journal. 16. The WHO operational handbook on drug-resistant TB treatment provides detailed guidelines on dosage by weight bands for medicines used in MDR-TB regimens for adults and children. 17. Conradi et al. evaluated the treatment of highly drug-resistant pulmonary TB, with their findings published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 18. The FDA approved pretomanid for use in the BPaL regimen (bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid) for treating MDR-TB, with details available on the FDA website. 19. Fox et al. conducted a meta-analysis on the role of surgery as an adjunctive treatment for MDR-TB, with findings published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 20. Kang et al. reviewed surgical treatment for MDR and XDR-TB, with their findings published in the Annals of Thoracic Surgery. 21. Harris et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the impact of surgery on MDR-TB treatment outcomes, published in BMC Infectious Diseases. 22. Chotmongkol et al. and Kumarvelu et al. studied the use of corticosteroids, such as dexamethasone, in tuberculous meningitis, with findings published in The Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand and Tubercle and Lung Disease, respectively. 23. Malhotra et al. compared dexamethasone and intravenous methylprednisolone in tuberculous meningitis, with findings published in Annals of Tropical Medicine and Parasitology. 24. Schoeman et al. 25. Thwaites et al. studied the use of dexamethasone in adolescents and adults with tuberculous meningitis, with findings published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 26. Critchley et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the role of corticosteroids in reducing mortality in tuberculosis, with findings published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 27. Hakim et al. and Mayosi et al. investigated the use of adjunctive prednisolone in tuberculous pericarditis, with findings published in Heart and the New England Journal of Medicine, respectively. 28. Reuter et al. and Strang et al. explored the use of corticosteroids and surgical drainage in managing tuberculous pericardial effusion, with findings published in Cardiovascular Journal of South Africa and The Lancet. 29. Skrahin et al. conducted a phase 1 safety trial on autologous mesenchymal stromal cell infusion as adjunctive therapy for MDR and XDR-TB, with findings published in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine. 30. Koh et al. and Park et al. studied the use of aerosolized and subcutaneously administered interferon-gamma in refractory MDR-TB, with findings published in the Journal of Korean Medical Science and International Journal of Infectious Diseases. 31. Suarez-Mendez et al. conducted a pilot study on the use of adjunctive interferon-gamma in drug-resistant pulmonary TB, with findings published in BMC Infectious Diseases. 32. Yang et al. evaluated the short-term efficacy of aerosolized recombinant human gamma interferon in MDR-TB, with findings published in the Journal of the Chinese Anti-Tuberculosis Association. 33. Wallis reviewed the lack of therapeutic benefit of interferon-gamma in tuberculosis, with findings published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases. 34. Alipanah et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on adherence interventions and outcomes in TB treatment, with findings published in PLOS Medicine. 35. Ho et al. reviewed decentralized care for MDR-TB, with findings published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 36. Cocozza et al. questioned whether effective patient support is missing in the global response to MDR-TB, with findings published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease. 37. The WHO operational handbook on drug-resistant TB treatment provides comprehensive guidelines on supportive care and dosage adjustments for MDR-TB regimens. 38. Campbell et al. emphasized the importance of improving patient data quality for MDR-TB treatment, with findings published in Emerging Infectious Diseases. 39. The WHO, in collaboration with other organizations, has developed international standards for TB care, including electronic recording and reporting systems. 40. The WHO guidelines on drug-resistant TB treatment are based on the latest reviews and best practices, incorporating pharmacokinetic modeling and allometric scaling to optimize dosing for MDR/RR-TB patients.
